description: Replace row-wise packed-sidecar expansion for both n=512 regimes with TMA swizzled gather and cluster multicast: publish each factor tile once, feed separate panel and update owners, retain accumulators across correction products, and directly scatter the lower factor while preserving the donor's owner DAG.

Replaced row-wise packed-sidecar triple staging in the batch640 N512 persistent path with one 2 KiB plus one contiguous 4 KiB cp.async.bulk transaction into packed shared buffers, followed by cooperative expansion into bank-padded LD40 MathDx operands while retaining paired FP32 accumulators. Build and full validation passed. The benchmark completed through batch16/N512 at 190.582 us, then the batch640 specialization hit an unspecified launch failure, so no complete aggregate metric was emitted.

Corrected the packed-triple mbarrier parity so each bulk transaction is waited on with its producing phase before cooperative LD40 expansion. Build and official validation passed, and the benchmark ran all 15 cells, but batch640/N512 produced NaN/Inf; batch16/N512 measured 190.713 us. The remaining fault is in packed bulk staging/expansion correctness rather than the barrier's initial parity.

Issued both packed bulk copies from lane 0 so mbarrier expect-tx and the contiguous 2 KiB/4 KiB transactions have a single producer. The full benchmark still reported NaN/Inf only for batch640/N512, with batch16/N512 at 190.780 us, so cross-lane issue ordering was not the remaining correctness fault.

Extended the dynamic shared half view to include the six packed 32x32 bulk-staging tiles before cooperative expansion. The complete benchmark passed at 775.041 us; batch16/N512 measured 190.809 us and batch640/N512 measured 1253.454 us. Correct bulk staging therefore adds substantial shared-memory/expansion cost versus the 1025.284 us parent high-batch cell.

Reused one three-tile packed bulk staging bank for both alternating LD40 operand banks, cutting extra dynamic shared memory from 12 KiB to 6 KiB while preserving the correction-product accumulator pipeline. The full benchmark passed at 775.382 us; batch640/N512 improved slightly from 1253.454 to 1243.275 us and batch16/N512 measured 190.178 us.

Best validated result in this brief was trial 3 commit f25aad5d2e58bdfdc3e7843319d2e69ef42d01e3 at 775.041 us full-grid, with batch16/N512=190.809 us and batch640/N512=1253.454 us; trial 4 reused one packed staging bank and measured 775.382 us / 1243.275 us. The parent remains 684.643 us with batch640/N512=1025.284 us. Trials 0-2 exposed and logged launch/parity/shared-view failures before the bulk path was corrected. The measured implementation replaces row-wise triple expansion with contiguous cp.async.bulk publication into packed shared followed by cooperative scatter to padded LD40 operands, but the extra packed shared footprint and scatter synchronize each correction stage. Open directions remain true TMA descriptor swizzle directly into the MathDx-consumable layout, cluster multicast between separate panel/update owners so one publication feeds multiple CTAs, and TMEM-resident correction operands/accumulators that eliminate the explicit packed-to-padded scatter. Continue from the parent for those variants; this branch records the working bulk-staging cost and failure modes.

Continue from the original 0b18f368 parent rather than the bulk-staging branch: implement a true TMA descriptor swizzle that lands directly in the MathDx-consumable padded layout, or cluster multicast one factor publication to separate panel/update owners. Avoid any explicit packed-to-padded scatter and use TMEM residency for correction accumulators where the descriptor path permits.

Continue from the original 0b18f368 parent rather than the bulk-staging branch: implement a true TMA descriptor swizzle that lands directly in the MathDx-consumable padded layout, or cluster multicast one factor publication to separate panel/update owners. Avoid any explicit packed-to-padded scatter and use TMEM residency for correction accumulators where the descriptor path permits.

Restarted from 0b18f368 and implemented a true 2D TMA descriptor path with LD40 global sidecars so three correction operands land directly in their final MathDx shared layout, with no packed-to-padded scatter. Build passed and the benchmark reached batch16/N512 at 190.633 us, but descriptor construction failed before batch640 because cuda-python requires typed cuuint32 element-stride objects rather than Python integers.

Fixed cuda-python tensor-map construction with typed dimensions and strides. Descriptor creation then succeeded, but Numba represented the aligned descriptor as a record pointer while the external TMA device function requires a uint64 pointer, so batch640 specialization failed during type inference after batch16 measured 190.674 us.

Represented the tensor-map descriptor as a uint64 array so the external device ABI matched. Numba then progressed to whole-kernel typing and exposed one mistakenly forwarded tensor-map argument on the non-TMA k=0 panel helper; batch16/N512 measured 190.866 us before specialization stopped.

Completed Numba typing and launched the direct LD40 TMA correction-loader kernel. The first batch640 invocation produced CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED after batch16/N512 measured 190.974 us. The likely launch fault is the descriptor being copied to device memory by Numba even though TMA instructions require the 128-byte descriptor in constant/parameter address space, not the sidecar coordinates or explicit scatter path.

Added the required GPU-scope tensormap proxy acquire before the three direct TMA loads. The first batch640 launch still failed with CUDA error 719 after batch16/N512 measured 191.021 us, so descriptor visibility fencing alone did not make Numba's temporary device descriptor a legal tensormap operand.

Moved the 128-byte tensor-map descriptor into aligned global storage in the linked CUDA module and copied the encoded descriptor there before launch. This removed the immediate CUDA launch fault, but the benchmark did not acquire a GPU within the measurement window and was interrupted after prolonged fleet lock contention before any active-set cell ran. The next revision also replaces inherited cp.async waits with mbarrier parity waits for the direct TMA correction stages.

Corrected synchronization so scalar cp.async helpers retain CTA synchronization while the two direct TMA correction-pair helpers wait on mbarrier parity. The descriptor path now launches across the active set and batch16/N512 measured 189.776 us, but batch640/N512 produced NaN/Inf, so this revision is recorded as a validation failure before changing descriptor lifetime handling.

Refreshed the linked-module TMA descriptor before every launch so each cached N512 sidecar allocation supplies its own base address. Full validation passed, batch16/N512 measured 190.782 us, but batch640/N512 still produced NaN/Inf; descriptor staleness across cached allocations was therefore fixed without resolving the large-batch correction corruption.

Corrected sidecar tile addressing to advance by the full 32x40 padded footprint rather than the inherited packed 32x32 shift. Full validation passed and batch16/N512 measured 190.512 us, but batch640/N512 still produced NaN/Inf, showing that removing factor-tile overlap alone did not resolve the TMA pipeline corruption.

Added a global async-proxy fence before every direct TMA correction prefetch so ordinary factor-sidecar stores become visible to the TMA proxy. Full validation passed and batch16/N512 measured 193.396 us, but batch640/N512 still produced NaN/Inf; proxy publication fencing did not remove the large-batch corruption.

Changed the final LD40 sidecar allocation to zero-initialize descriptor-visible padding lanes. Validation passed because its N512 batches do not select this path, but the active benchmark stopped at batch640 allocation: torch.zeros rejects the inherited memory_format argument. Batch16/N512 measured 192.801 us before the runtime error.

Fixed the zero-initialized LD40 sidecar allocation so all eight padding columns are defined without an intermediate layout or scatter. Full validation passed and batch16/N512 measured 190.748 us, but batch640/N512 still produced NaN/Inf; uninitialized MathDx padding was not the source of corruption.

Made the padded TMA sidecar and tensor-map descriptor shape-scoped so asynchronous launches cannot race by rewriting one module-global descriptor to different cached allocations. Full validation passed and batch16/N512 measured 190.635 us, but batch640/N512 still produced NaN/Inf; descriptor-base races between cached inputs were removed without fixing the correction result.

Moved the TMA mbarrier state after six explicitly reserved correction operand banks to test shared-state overlap. The official batch640/N512 single-shape check still produced NaN/Inf; this also exposed that the original float32-sliced update region already represented six FP16 banks, so doubling its float32 extent was not the correct fix.

Placed the aligned 128-byte tensor map in linked-module constant storage rather than ordinary device-global storage. The official batch640/N512 single-shape check still produced NaN/Inf, so descriptor storage class alone did not correct the direct TMA result.

Added the CCCL-prescribed fence.proxy.async.shared::cta immediately after mbarrier initialization so TMA completion can observe the barrier through the async proxy. The official batch640/N512 single-shape check still produced NaN/Inf.

Reinitialized and re-published the mbarrier after every completed TMA triple, always waiting parity zero, to remove phase-reuse ambiguity while retaining direct LD40 tensor transfers. The official batch640/N512 single-shape check still produced NaN/Inf.

Updated the retained single- and pair-factor cp.async consumers from packed LD32 to the same direct LD40 sidecar layout used by TMA. This removed the batch640 corruption: full validation and all 15 active benchmark shapes passed. Batch640/N512 measured 2048.713 us and the aggregate metric was 805.037 us; batch16/N512 remains on its separate kernel at 190.819 us.

Restored alternating mbarrier parity reuse after correcting every sidecar consumer to LD40. All active shapes passed; batch640/N512 improved from the one-shot-barrier trial's 2048.713 us to 2014.423 us, and the aggregate metric improved from 805.037 us to 803.196 us.

Removed the per-triple global async-proxy fence and CTA synchronization while retaining the required tensormap acquire and shared-barrier proxy publication. All active shapes passed; batch640/N512 improved from 2014.423 us to 1963.699 us and the aggregate metric improved from 803.196 us to 798.417 us.

Cached the tensor-map identity so the identical 128-byte constant descriptor is uploaded only when the shape-scoped sidecar changes, not before every launch. All active shapes passed; batch640/N512 improved from 1963.699 us to 1928.038 us, while cross-shape timing variance moved the aggregate from 798.417 us to 802.132 us.

Restarted from parent 0b18f368 and implemented a true 2D TMA path whose LD40 sidecar maps directly into the MathDx-consumable padded shared layout, with no packed-to-padded scatter. The working path uses a constant-memory tensor map, required tensormap and shared async-proxy fences, alternating mbarrier parity, shape-scoped descriptor storage, and LD40 semantics for every retained factor consumer. The key correctness issue was that non-TMA single/pair cp.async factor loads still used packed LD32 after publication changed to LD40. Trials 22-25 passed all 15 active shapes. Best aggregate was trial 24 at 798.417 us; final trial 25 measured 802.132 us overall and the lowest batch640/N512 result in this pass at 1928.038 us, versus parent 1025.284 us for that cell and parent aggregate 684.643 us. The final SHA-named nsys profile shows _dx_potrf at 1.720 ms. Concrete remaining directions are cluster multicast with separate panel/update owners to expose inter-CTA parallelism, replacing the residual single/pair cp.async consumers with descriptor loads to remove mixed transport, and TMEM-resident correction accumulation so factor updates do not round-trip through the six shared operand banks.
